A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the paper disc assay method using B. cereus was the best procedure to detect the 3 tectracycline antibiotics, penicillin and zinc bacitracins, whilst S. lutea was the best organism for detecting the remaining antibiotics at the minimum levels of detection.
the two paper disc assay methods are simple, rapid, sensitive and specific and are useful in detecting residues of antibiotics in meat and other animal products.
the first paper disc assay method could detect all the antibiotics at levels below the FAO/WHO permitted maximum permissible level in muscle, except for streptomycin and spiramycin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both the paper disc assay methods are simple and reliable for screening for antibiotic residues in meat.
the use of B. cereus and S. lutea in the paper disc assay procedure is not sufficient for detecting all antibiotics at the levels permitted for meat for human use.
the use of the B. cereus assay method is sufficient to meet the FAO/WHO requirements.
